history.period: Ancient (local tradition); exact founding date UNVERIFIED
history.summary: The Someshwar Temple at Someshwar, on the banks of the Godavari at Gangapur Road about 7-8 km west of Nashik city, is regarded as one of the oldest Shiva shrines of Nashik, though no inscription or record establishes its exact age (UNVERIFIED). Local belief holds that Lord Shiva in the form of Someshwar Mahadev visited Nashik to bless the region, and that the Godavari's flow here is linked to his divine intervention. The temple has undergone renovations over the centuries but retains its riverside character; the adjacent Someshwar (Dudhsagar) waterfall on the Godavari is a popular seasonal attraction beside it. Boating facilities and a small children's park on the premises make it a combined pilgrimage-picnic destination.

name: Someshwar Temple
town_description: Nashik, on the banks of the Godavari, is one of India's holiest cities and host of the Kumbh Mela every 12 years, famed for the Panchavati quarter's Ramayana sites, Ramkund and the Godavari ghats. The Someshwar suburb lies on the city's western edge along Gangapur Road, a greener, quieter riverside stretch known for the Someshwar temple and waterfall. Nashik is also a major wine (Sula Vineyards) and agricultural trade centre.

travel.railway: Nashik Road Railway Station (approx. 10-12 km; 20-25 minutes by taxi per visitor guides)
travel.road: On Gangapur Road about 7-8 km west of Nashik city centre; autos, taxis and city buses serve the area; ample parking nearby.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March for pleasant weather; September-February recommended for the waterfall flow after monsoon; Maha Shivratri and Shravan are the festive peaks.
